original_question: Consider the cardinality-based 4-uniform hypergraph s-t cut problem in which every 1-vs-3 hyperedge split has penalty w_1 = 1 and every 2-vs-2 split has penalty w_2. What is the computational complexity of this problem in the regime w_2 > 2?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Open Problem 3.1: determine the complexity of the cardinality-based 4-uniform hypergraph s-t cut problem in the regime w2 > 2 after normalizing w1 = 1.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's intended target almost exactly: it identifies the cardinality-based 4-uniform hypergraph s-t cut problem, fixes the 1-vs-3 split penalty to w1 = 1, asks about the regime w2 > 2, and asks for the computational complexity. This is essentially a paraphrase of Open Problem 3.1.
missing_details: The input should be stated explicitly: an arbitrary 4-uniform hypergraph H = (V, E) with a distinguished source node s and sink node t.
A feasible solution is a bipartition {S, V minus S} with s in S and t in V minus S.
The paper defines split classes by ∂_i(S) = {e in E : min(|e ∩ S|, |e ∩ (V minus S)|) = i}; in the 4-uniform case, only i = 1 and i = 2 can occur for cut hyperedges, and w0 = 0.
The optimization objective should be written explicitly as minimizing |∂_1(S)| + w2|∂_2(S)| over all feasible S.
It should be explicit that w2 is a fixed real penalty shared by all hyperedges, and the open problem asks for a complexity classification across the regime of fixed values w2 > 2.
The normalization w1 = 1 is justified only under the assumption w1 > 0, since the paper rescales parameters without loss of generality in that case.

The draft does not mention that the paper separately introduces the limit case w2 → ∞ as Open Problem 3.2 (the No-Even-Split 4-uniform s-t cut problem), which is a special case and not the same question.
refined_question: For an arbitrary 4-uniform hypergraph H = (V, E) with distinguished vertices s and t, define for each feasible cut S ⊆ V with s in S and t in V minus S the sets ∂_i(S) = {e ∈ E : min(|e ∩ S|, |e ∩ (V minus S)|) = i}. After the without-loss-of-generality normalization w1 = 1 (for w1 > 0), the cardinality-based hypergraph s-t cut problem is to minimize |∂_1(S)| + w2|∂_2(S)| over all such S. What is the computational complexity of this optimization problem for fixed penalty parameters w2 > 2?
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper's official formulation. In Section 3, the paper first summarizes the known threshold behavior for 4-uniform hypergraph s-t cuts: NP-hardness for 0 ≤ w2 < 1, polynomial-time solvability for 1 ≤ w2 ≤ 2, and an open status for w2 > 2. It then defines the cardinality-based objective formally via equation (1) using the sets ∂_i(S), notes that for 4-uniform hypergraphs one may scale parameters so that w1 = 1 whenever w1 > 0, and states Open Problem 3.1 in essentially the same words as your draft. The nearby Open Problem 3.2 is only a suggested limit-case special case (No-Even-Split 4-uniform s-t cut), so the sharp paper-faithful target is Open Problem 3.1 rather than that neighboring variant.
